grandparents_cupboard.reason: Parsnips, onion, spinach, eggs, cheddar, rocket, oil, thyme and nutmeg are all plain kitchen staples with nothing factory-made.

supermarket.reason: Every ingredient is an everyday Tesco item at a normal price.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a lidded non-stick frying pan, a grater and a bowl, and cooking a frittata on the hob under a lid is well within a beginner's reach.

works.reason: Eight eggs, three grated parsnips, spinach and 75g cheddar make a well-seasoned frittata for four, and a covered low heat will set it without needing a grill.

honest_times.reason: Fifteen minutes is enough to peel and grate the parsnips, slice the onion and grate the cheese, and the 20 cook minutes are only slightly under the 8 minutes frying plus 12 to 15 minutes setting in the steps.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning is used in the steps, the names match their ids, and fresh thyme is on the October list.

seasonal_feel.reason: Grated parsnip is the bulk of the frittata, which makes a warm, simple lunch that suits early October.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, clear British English instructions with no restaurant language or preaching.

hearty_healthy.reason: Eggs, cheese, parsnips, spinach and rocket make a filling, balanced lunch a family would happily eat again.
